## High-Frequency Sensor Network: Poudre Reach

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="48%"}

::: {.ross-card}
### Diagnostic Baseline for Settlement Reach

**Target Corridor:** Cache la Poudre River from above the *Munroe Gravity Canal Diversion* down to the *South Platte River Confluence*.

::: {.callout-note icon=false}
#### Core Thesis
Continuous high-frequency sensors provide the empirical diagnostic baseline needed to evaluate restoration performance **before a single dollar is spent**.
:::

- **Parameters Tracked:** Water Temperature, Dissolved Oxygen, Turbidity, & Nitrate ($\text{NO}_3^-$)
- **Accountability:** Unassailable data across urban & agricultural reaches
- **Empirical Rigor:** Performance evaluated by downstream mass balance, not visual assumptions

[Dr. Matthew Ross | ROSS Lab]{.presenter-badge}
:::

:::

::: {.column width="52%"}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| fig-height: 5.5
#| out-width: "100%"

library(leaflet)

stations <- data.frame(
  id = 1:10,
  name = c(
    "Munroe Gravity Canal Diversion",
    "Poudre Canyon Mouth (USGS 06752000)",
    "Bellvue / Watson Lake Reach",
    "Laporte Sentinel Site",
    "Fort Collins Downtown (USGS 06752260)",
    "Environmental Learning Center (ELC)",
    "Timnath Reach",
    "Windsor Reach (USGS 06752280)",
    "Greeley O Street Bridge (USGS 06752400)",
    "South Platte Confluence (USGS 06752500)"
  ),
  type = c("Boundary", "Sensor Station", "Sensor Station", "Sensor Station", "Sensor Station", 
           "Sensor Station", "Sensor Station", "Sensor Station", "Sensor Station", "Outlet Boundary"),
  lat = c(40.6970, 40.6912, 40.6300, 40.6270, 40.5885, 40.5530, 40.5280, 40.4780, 40.4420, 40.4180),
  lng = c(-105.2150, -105.1950, -105.1720, -105.1400, -105.0690, -105.0120, -104.9750, -104.9120, -104.6780, -104.6020),
  params = c("Diversion Intake", "Flow, Temp, Turbidity", "Temp, DO, Turbidity", "Temp, DO, NO3-", "Flow, Temp, DO, NO3-",
             "Temp, DO, SpCond", "Temp, DO, NO3-", "Flow, Temp, DO, NO3-", "Flow, Temp, DO, NO3-", "Outlet Mass Balance")
)

getColor <- function(t) {
  ifelse(grepl("Boundary", t), "#d97706", "#0284c7")
}

river_coords <- matrix(c(
  -105.2150, 40.6970,
  -105.1950, 40.6912,
  -105.1720, 40.6300,
  -105.1400, 40.6270,
  -105.0690, 40.5885,
  -105.0120, 40.5530,
  -104.9750, 40.5280,
  -104.9120, 40.4780,
  -104.6780, 40.4420,
  -104.6020, 40.4180
), ncol = 2, byrow = TRUE)

leaflet(stations) %>%
  addTiles(urlTemplate = "https://{s}.basemaps.cartocdn.com/rastertiles/voyager/{z}/{x}/{y}{r}.png") %>%
  addPolylines(lng = river_coords[,1], lat = river_coords[,2], color = "#0284c7", weight = 5, opacity = 0.85) %>%
  addCircleMarkers(
    lng = ~lng, lat = ~lat,
    radius = 8,
    color = getColor(stations$type),
    fillColor = getColor(stations$type),
    fillOpacity = 0.9,
    popup = paste0("<b>", stations$name, "</b><br/>", stations$params)
  )
```

## Core Principle: Restoration Without Monitoring is Greenwashing

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}

::: {.callout-warning icon=false}
### The Unmonitored Pitfall

- **Millions Spent Annually:** Instream structural fixes (BDAs, boulder clusters, Stage 0 channel reshapes) are heavily promoted in gravel snowmelt rivers.
- **Flawed Metrics:** Success is measured by *inputs* ("dollars spent") and *outputs* ("feet of bank shaped on Day 1").
- **5-Year Performance Gap:** Without continuous monitoring, interventions fail to show downstream water quality or ecosystem gains.
- **Settlement Risk:** Investing in unmonitored channel restructuring risks capital loss without verifiable reach-scale improvements.
:::

:::

::: {.column width="50%"}

::: {.callout-tip icon=false}
### The Empirical Alternative

- **Continuous Sensor Arrays:** Automated real-time sensors measuring Water Temperature, Dissolved Oxygen, Turbidity, and Nitrate.
- **Why Grab Samples Fail:** Sparse monthly grab samples miss >90% of storm runoff events, pulse loads, and acute summer thermal stress.
- **Transparent Mass Balance:** Converts subjective claims into hard, unassailable downstream data.
- **Guiding Rule:** Continuous monitoring protects committee capital and guarantees fiduciary accountability.
:::

:::
:::

## Downstream Water Quality Impact Matrix

<table class="matrix-table">
  <thead>
    <tr>
      <th style="width: 18%;">Technique</th>
      <th style="width: 24%;">Physical Mechanism</th>
      <th style="width: 20%;">Downstream WQ Evidence</th>
      <th style="width: 20%;">Long-Term Viability</th>
      <th style="width: 18%;">Primary Citations</th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr>
      <td><strong>Dam / Diversion Removal &amp; Retrofits</strong></td>
      <td>Restores longitudinal connectivity, natural sediment transport, &amp; thermal regime.</td>
      <td><span class="badge badge-high">HIGH EVIDENCE</span><br/>Eliminates local temp spikes, re-oxygenates, clears fine sediment.</td>
      <td>Permanent solution. Highest ROI per linear km.</td>
      <td class="citation">Bednarek (2001)<br/>Doyle et al. (2005)<br/>Bernhardt &amp; Palmer (2011)</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td><strong>Active Riparian Canopy (Willow/Cottonwood)</strong></td>
      <td>Solar radiation shading, bank root cohesion, hyporheic nutrient uptake.</td>
      <td><span class="badge badge-high">HIGH (THERMAL)</span><br/>Consistent 1–3°C drop in max summer water temps. Moderate NO3⁻ interception.</td>
      <td>High durability once established; self-sustaining.</td>
      <td class="citation">Poole &amp; Berman (2001)<br/>Caissie (2006)<br/>Kalny et al. (2017)</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td><strong>Floodplain &amp; Side-Channel Reconnection</strong></td>
      <td>Attenuates peak flood energy, drops TSS, expands hyporheic residence.</td>
      <td><span class="badge badge-mod">MODERATE</span><br/>High TSS &amp; NO3⁻ settling during flood peaks; negligible during baseflows.</td>
      <td>High viability if high-flow flood hydrograph remains intact.</td>
      <td class="citation">Opperman et al. (2010)<br/>Noe et al. (2013)<br/>Kaushal et al. (2008)</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td><strong>In-Stream Reconfiguration (ELJs, Boulders)</strong></td>
      <td>Creates localized velocity refuge, scour pools, &amp; physical trout habitat.</td>
      <td><span class="badge badge-low">LOW / NEGLIGIBLE</span><br/>High local physical habitat score; zero downstream nutrient/thermal impact.</td>
      <td>Vulnerable to destruction during 10-year snowmelt runoff events.</td>
      <td class="citation">Palmer et al. (2005, 2010)<br/>Bernhardt et al. (2005)<br/>Filoso &amp; Palmer (2011)</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td><strong>Beaver Dam Analogues (BDAs)</strong></td>
      <td>Aggrades channel, forces overbank flooding, elevates alluvial water table.</td>
      <td><span class="badge badge-mixed">MIXED / CONDITIONAL</span><br/>Local TSS drop, but frequently spikes summer max temps (solar ponding) &amp; releases Ortho-P.</td>
      <td>High failure rate in high-energy gravel rivers without real beavers.</td>
      <td class="citation">Weber et al. (2017)<br/>Lautz et al. (2013)<br/>Majerova et al. (2015)</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td><strong>Stage 0 / Process-Based Restoration</strong></td>
      <td>Spreads flow into unconfined multi-thread wetland complexes.</td>
      <td><span class="badge badge-low">UNPROVEN WQ</span><br/>High local habitat value in low-energy valley bottoms; unproven for downstream export.</td>
      <td>Requires huge land footprint; high evaporative loss.</td>
      <td class="citation">Cluer &amp; Thorne (2014)<br/>Powers et al. (2019)<br/>Kondolf et al. (2006)</td>
    </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>

::: {.callout-note icon=false}
**Peer-Reviewed Finding:** Comprehensive national reviews (*Bernhardt et al. 2005; Palmer et al. 2010*) reveal that over 90% of in-stream structural restoration projects perform zero post-project monitoring. Structural channel reconfigurations create local physical structure, but **only thermal shading, barrier removal, and flow preservation alter downstream water quality mass balance**.
:::

## Mindful Stewardship & Risk Mitigation ($100M Settlement)

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}

::: {.ross-card}
### The "3% Sentinel Rule"

Institute a mandatory policy requiring every funded capital project to dedicate **3% to 5% of its total budget** to automated continuous sensor monitoring.

- **Pre- & Post-Implementation:** 12-month pre-project baseline and 3-year post-project continuous tracking.
- **Continuous Telemetry:** Automated stations deployed immediately upstream & downstream of project reaches.
- **Beyond Grab Samples:** Eliminates reliance on monthly grab samples that miss high-flow events and thermal spikes.
:::

:::

::: {.column width="50%"}

::: {.ross-card}
### Fiduciary Protection for Committee

1. **Unassailable Accountability:** Empirical proof of performance demonstrating ROI to stakeholders and regulators.
2. **Early Risk Mitigation:** Identifies underperforming or failing structural interventions before capital is wasted.
3. **Shield Against Greenwashing:** Defends committee funding choices with open, real-time science-backed data.
:::

:::
:::

## Direct Answers to Committee Questions

::: {.qa-grid}

::: {.qa-card}
::: {.qa-title}
1. Incorporate Monitoring Mindfully?
:::
::: {.qa-body}
Enforce the **3% Sentinel Rule**. Mandate 3–5% budget allocation for automated continuous sensors (Temp, DO, $\text{NO}_3^-$, Turbidity) over sparse monthly grab samples.
:::
:::

::: {.qa-card}
::: {.qa-title}
2. Investment Dollars Strategy?
:::
::: {.qa-body}
Prioritize **low-maintenance, permanent returns** (flow preservation, canopy shading, diversion retrofits) over high-maintenance structural channel fixes.
:::
:::

::: {.qa-card}
::: {.qa-title}
3. Prioritizing 5 Criteria?
:::
::: {.qa-body}
Focus on **Water Flows & Aquatic Habitat via Barrier Removal**. Eliminating diversion barriers between Munroe Canal & South Platte solves passage, thermal & habitat bottlenecks together.
:::
:::

::: {.qa-card}
::: {.qa-title}
4. Best Projects for Flow Regime?
:::
::: {.qa-body}
**Diversion consolidation, seasonal water-sharing leases, and automated bypass gates**. Physical channel tweaks cannot compensate for missing late-summer water.
:::
:::

::: {.qa-card}
::: {.qa-title}
5. Committee's Biggest Bang for Buck?
:::
::: {.qa-body}
**Riparian Canopy Re-establishment & Diversion Bypass Retrofits**. Native willow/cottonwood shading yields guaranteed thermal drops (1–3°C) at a fraction of heavy equipment cost.
:::
:::

::: {.qa-card}
::: {.qa-title}
6. Key Stakeholders to Engage?
:::
::: {.qa-body}
**Ditch Companies & Open Hydroinformatics Groups**. Engage irrigation ditch companies (for flow consolidation opportunities) and independent open-data hydroinformatics teams.
:::
:::
